content.text: : block late-phase reaction to the allergen, reduce airway hyperresponsiveness, & they are potent/effective anti-inflammatory medications
•reduce sxs, increase lung function, improve QOL, & reduce risk of exacerbations
: first line for all pts w/ persistent asthma; they are the most effective anti-inflammatory agents
: high doses for prolonged periods may cause adrenal suppression, increase risk of fractures, & stunted growth in children
: short-course for acute exacerbations or not properly responding to tx; taper over 1wk
: indicated in acute asthma if lung function is <30% predicted & in pts who show no significant improvement w/ nebulized beta-2 agonist
•oral: during exacerbations or severe asthma that is difficult to control even w/ combination medications
•limit use to avoid risk of adverse effects
: short-acting beta-2 agonist; binding at beta-2 receptors causes relaxation of bronchial smooth muscles & bronchodilation
: all pts w/ asthma get one
: nervousness, tremor, tachycardia, palpitations, cough, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia

•used in combination w/ ICS (never as monotherapy)
: nervousness, tremor, tachycardia, palpitations, cough, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia
: increase risk of asthma-related deaths and should only be used in asthma patients who are on a long-term asthma control medication (ICS), but are not adequately controlled
: inhibit leukotriene mediators of airway inflammation; help decrease airway edema, constriction, & inflammation
: alternative option to LABA for add-on therapy to ICS; can also be added to ICS + LABA therapy

: blocks phosphodiesterase, causing increase in cAMP and release of EPI from adrenal medulla cells. Results in bronchodilation, but also causes diuresis, CNS and cardiac stimulation, and gastric acid secretion
: least desirable option of add-on treatment due to significant ADRs, drug interactions, & the need to monitor drug concentrations
: N/V, HA, tachycardia, insomnia, tremor, nervousness
: may exacerbate CVD, hyperthyroidism, PUD, & seizure disorders
: typically reserved for pts who cannot take beta-2 agonists
•inhibits IgE binding to the IgE receptor on mast cells and basophils. Prevents activation by asthma trigger antigens and subsequent release of inflammatory mediators
•Histamine, prostaglandins, and leukotrienes are unable to cause sneezing, coughing, wheezing, and itching

•Tiotropium: only LAMA approved for asthma; may be used as additional therapy in pts ≥6yo who are uncontrolled on ICS/LABA therapy
